summary: The glymphatic constitutes a crucial neurophysiological mechanism for the clearance of interstitial solutes and neurotoxic metabolites from the central nervous system. Advanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) modalities, such as diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), have emerged as non-invasive, in vivo approaches quantifying glymphatic transport efficacy and its association with cognitive decline and AD progression. title: Scn1a-mediated developmental regulation of prefrontal cortex plasticity and cognition.
summary: The voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.1, encoded by Scn1a, is essential for γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic function, and its alteration is associated with neurological disorders such as Dravet syndrome and Alzheimer's disease. summary: Based on an edge-centric functional network model, this study investigated the longitudinal evolution of overlapping network structures after mild traumatic brain injury and explored their potential molecular basis through transcriptomic analysis. summary: Background: Telemedicine offers promising tools for migraine care and research. title: Older adults in more disadvantaged neighborhoods exhibit brain vascular dysfunction.
summary: Neighborhood disadvantage is a risk factor for dementia, but the mechanisms involved are not well understood. In this study, we explored the relationship between neighborhood deprivation and whole-brain cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) in 132 older adults without a history of clinical stroke or dementia. Participants underwent brain MRI and venipuncture. Relative neighborhood deprivation was quantified using the Area Deprivation Index. title: Case Report: Clinical and magnetic resonance imaging findings in intracranial hemangiosarcoma in a cat.
summary: Hemangiosarcoma (HSA) is a highly malignant tumor of endothelial origin that is infrequently reported in cats, accounting for less than 2% of nonhematopoietic neoplasms. Feline HSA is typically classified into dermal and visceral subtypes, both of which exhibit metastatic potential. While HSA is the tumor most commonly reported to metastasize to the brain in dogs, intracranial involvement in cats remains rare, with only one previously documented metastatic case. This case report details the clinical presentation, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features, histopathological findings, and gross post-mortem brain changes in a cat diagnosed with intracranial hemangiosarcoma.

title: Advances in MRI of glymphatic system dysfunction associated with obstructive sleep apnea and enlarged perivascular spaces.

summary: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) are an indolent subset of neuroendocrine neoplasms with a propensity to metastasize. summary: Stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG)-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC) has emerged as a minimally invasive treatment option for selected patients with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). summary: Age-related declines in lower-limb somatosensory function may contribute to impaired motor control and increased fall risk in older adults. title: Resting-state frontal theta/beta ratio and psychological symptoms in college students: an EEG study.
summary: Mental health problems are increasingly prevalent among college students and represent an important public health concern. title: Neurocognitive mechanisms of source credibility: how work experience and patient ratings modulate the processing of medical veracity cues.
summary: Source credibility is fundamental to how medical information is processed,yet the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms remain poorly understood.
